chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Richard's patent for a dive-bomber machine gun
summary: A 1940 patent for a machine gun on ball bearings so a dive bomber could fire in any direction.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Now, let's see what else he's got here. Now, this, I told you, was the gun. See, it says, "Richard B. Spikes..." What does it say there?
Uh, the address is 5 North Center Street, Stockton, California...
And, "Machine-gun, Richard B. Spikes, inventor. A machine-gun for dive bombers," it says.

Yeah, this fits on, you know, I told you that used to have the old gun that when the airplane would shoot you this way and then they'd have to go 'way around and turn around back and shoot your gun. It was stationary. So he built it on balls and bearin... ball-bearings so that when you pass, you could shoot you this way, and when he turns his back, while he's leaving you, he's shooting thisaway, and when he's shooting coming, you're turned all away around --the gun. He could shoot you from any position.
Is there a date on this one?
Yeah, must be..."Spikes, 23rd day of September, '40, City of Washington, D.C." It's called what? "Automatic...
"...Machine-gun." And then it says, "For dive bombers and aerial attack." He was a busy man.
